The thermite reduction of manganese dioxide by aluminium is a named extraction route for a medium-reactivity metal - LO-6. It is not a salt-solution displacement, so LO-2's predictive clause is not the demand.
The assertion defines the activity series (LO-2). The reason borrows LO-1 language about telling metals from non-metals, but the item's key turns on that reason being false, so LO-1 is not co-cited.
Extraction method for top-of-series metals. LO-6 names the low/medium/high reactivity bands itself, so it carries this item alone without help from LO-2.

Alloying to improve a metal's properties - the one alloy idea LO-7 actually reaches. Straight definition of corrosion - the 'explains corrosion' half of LO-7, with no prevention method involved.

Scoring this requires knowing the real cause of silver blackening is sulphur in the air, not low reactivity - a corrosion-mechanism judgement (LO-7). LO-2 was rejected because the reactivity claim in the reason is precisely the distractor.

Which metals resist corrosion; the subject is corrosion, so LO-7, even though nobility is the underlying selector. DEFECT: the stored answer lists silver as not corroding easily, contradicting four other items in this same chapter that teach silver tarnishing to Ag2S.
Electrical conductivity of copper as the reason for its use in wiring - a physical property of metals (LO-1).
Names a metal that corrodes in the atmosphere. A corrosion item (LO-7); it asks what corrodes, not how metals rank in reactivity.

Zinc displacing iron from iron(II) sulphate - a series prediction (LO-2). DEFECT: the marked key is 'Assertion false but Reason true', while the printed reason ('zinc is less reactive than iron') is false and the item's own explanation says so; the correct option is 'both false'.
Tarnishing of silver and the identity of the surface film - corrosion (LO-7). Kept apart from the LO-1 'metal reacts with X' items because the process is slow surface attack in air.

The whole judgement is whether zinc outranks tin and what follows for food cans - relative reactivity (LO-2). The tin coating is a corrosion barrier, but the item never asks about corrosion, only about the ranking.
Green basic copper carbonate in humid air - corrosion product identification (LO-7). Three alternative wordings of the same item are stored in one row.
The reason, 'non-metals form acidic oxides', is the classification rule of LO-1; the assertion fails only because carbon monoxide is neutral. Entirely a metal/non-metal chemical-property item.
Corrosion as a self-protecting surface layer. Still LO-7's 'explains corrosion' clause, approached from its useful side rather than as damage to be prevented.
States that reactivity with water and acids varies with position in the series - the ordering clause of LO-2, not any single metal's reaction.
Identifies both the corroding metal and the black corrosion product from a description - LO-7. The demand is the corrosion product, not a classification of silver as a metal.
Dulling of zinc explained by a basic-carbonate film in moist air - a corrosion mechanism with its equation, so LO-7 rather than a single-metal reaction under LO-1.
Pairs the melting-point exceptions on both sides of the classification (gallium low, diamond high) - precisely the property-based metal/non-metal sorting of LO-1.
